input.question: Why are general ed classes in college required regardless of your major?
input.ground_truth: The goal of college wasn't supposed to be just a job training program. It was meant to make you an educated person with a focus in a field, not to just literally do job training that you have to pay for. They have technical schools if you just want to specifically learn a craft or trade and not worry about general education.

Question: Why are general ed classes in college required regardless of your major?

Okay! Imagine you really love drawing, and you want to be an artist when you grow up. So, you go to "art school" to learn how to draw even better. But, before you can draw all day, you also need to know some important things, like how to read and write, how to add numbers, and how to talk to other people. These are things everyone needs to know, no matter what they want to do when they grow up.

That’s why colleges make you take "general education" classes. They help you learn lots of different things so you can be good at many parts of life, not just the one thing you love most. It’s like making sure you have all the pieces of a puzzle, not just the fun ones!
